content.text:
I submitted **index 3** (Sb fraction 0.353) as the best composition. Its EQE of 0.073% was the highest of the five I measured, and all five EQE measurements are used.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.280 | 0.043 |
| **3** | **0.353** | **0.073** |
| 4 | 0.383 | 0.055 |
| 8 | 0.513 | 0.018 |
| 13 | 0.659 | 0.0005 |

- **Where the peak is:** EQE is highest on the Pb-rich side, below the Sb fraction of Pb₂Sb₂O₇ (0.5). The model predicts a band gap of about 2.5 eV for Pb₂Sb₂O₇, which is below the 2.7 eV light used, so it should absorb.
- **Sb-rich side:** EQE falls steadily as Sb increases and is near zero at 0.66, close to PbSb₂O₆. That phase's predicted gap (about 2.7 eV) sits right at the light energy. I didn't measure anything above 0.66 Sb because of that trend.
- **Last measurement:** a curve through the first three points put the peak at about 0.38 Sb. I spent the last measurement there (index 4), but it came in lower (0.055%), so index 3 stayed the best.

Index 2 (Sb 0.325), next to the best point, was never measured, so the true maximum could be a little off index 3. I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements, so which phases are actually present is unconfirmed. The Gaussian-process suggestion tool was no help: it only proposed the unexplored Sb-rich end, where the trend already pointed to low EQE.
